claims.claim: Configuration Schema has a Tool section at /arena/reference/config-schema/#tool and the schema lives at schemas/v1alpha1/tool.json
mode values are mock, live, mcp, exec, client
mock (static) requires mock_result
mock (template) uses mock_template or mock_template_file
live mode requires an http: block
mcp mode needs no further fields; tool is exposed by an MCP server configured at the arena level and auto-discovered
exec mode requires an exec: block (tool shells out to a local subprocess)
client mode requires a client: block
mock_result and mock_template are mutually exclusive on a single tool
Static mock example (get-weather) is valid Tool YAML with metadata.name, spec.name, description, mode, timeout_ms, input_schema, output_schema, mock_result
Static mock returns the same response for every call
Args are parsed as a JSON map and exposed as the template data context; the rendered output is parsed back as JSON
The template executor already exists, so no custom executor is needed for input-branching mocks
Input-branching example (lookup-order) is valid Tool YAML
mock_template is rendered with Go text/template using Option("missingkey=zero")
The args map is the data context so .order_id accesses the call's order_id field
if/else if/else/end and range control flow are supported
Comparison helpers eq, ne, lt, gt, le, ge are available
printf, index and the rest of the standard template functions are available
{{- ... -}} trims surrounding whitespace so rendered output parses as JSON
mock_template_file points at a file whose path is relative to the tool YAML
mock_template_file example (spec: mode: mock, mock_template_file: templates/lookup-order.tmpl) is valid
mock_parts returns image/audio/video/document content alongside JSON and works with both mock_result and mock_template
Full mock_parts structure is documented in Configuration Schema -> Tool
Live mode calls a real HTTP endpoint; args are sent as JSON and the response is the parsed JSON body
http fields url, method, headers, headers_from_env, timeout_ms, redact exist
headers_from_env: [API_TOKEN] sets "Authorization: Bearer ${API_TOKEN}"
http.redact lists fields stripped from logs
http.timeout_ms: 5000 bounds the request
Live example YAML (spec fragment) is valid
For mcp mode, the Tool YAML only declares the contract and the MCP client provides the executor
mcp example (spec: mode: mcp) is valid
Exec mode calls a local subprocess; args on stdin, response read from stdout
Exec example (mode: exec, exec.command, exec.args, exec.timeout_ms) is valid
Client mode hands the tool call back to the SDK consumer or external system for execution
client fields timeout_ms, categories, consent (required, message, decline_strategy), validate_output exist
decline_strategy: error is a valid value
Client example YAML is valid
Diagram: deterministic fixture + same response -> mock + mock_result
Diagram: response depends on args -> mock + mock_template
Diagram: HTTP API -> live + http
Diagram: Tool from an MCP server -> mcp
Diagram: Local CLI or script -> exec
Diagram: Caller SDK or app handles it -> client
examples/voice-refund-demo uses mock_template branching across three personas, linked at github.com/AltairaLabs/promptarena/v2/tree/main/examples/voice-refund-demo
examples/customer-support uses mode: mock with static results, linked at github.com/AltairaLabs/promptarena/v2/tree/main/examples/customer-support
